thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — seeing a weird spike: EMEA traffic getting routed to aux-us-west after the variant-fallback rollout. Not expected. Anyone else?

mira: I saw that in the routing metrics dashboard, weird latency bump too. Can you dump a sample request id? :eyes:

alex: sample req: 0f8c3a. From EU tenant t-907. Timeline: primary model hit capacity, fallback kicked in, but routing sent it to aux-us-west instead of aux-eu.

sam: Are we sure it's the fallback policy and not a region preference bug? The policy code path changed last week.

infra-bot: alert: cross_region_fallback_rate for aux-us-west > 4% (5m window)

ops-oncall: tagging @mira @sam. I'm putting the service in read-only->local route for tier=trial customers while we triage.

mira: Can you paste the routing decision logs for req 0f8c3a? I want the policy evaluation trace.

alex: paste logs:

```
[2026-03-17T10:12:03Z] req=0f8c3a tenant=t-907 route=chat.generate
policy_eval: prefer_region=EU, tier=standard, model_variants=[m1-eu,m1-us-quant]
capacity_check: m1-eu: saturated(0.98), m1-eu-quant: saturated(0.92)
fallback_candidates: [m1-us-quant, m1-eu-2]
score(m1-us-quant)=0.78 (latency_penalty -0.2, cost_bonus +0.05)
chose m1-us-quant -> route target aux-us-west
```

mira: ah — capacity_check marks m1-eu as saturated at 0.98, but we intentionally treat anything <1.0 as usable for low-latency traffic. Looks like the comparator changed to >= instead of > in the last patch.

sam: that comparator change was part of the continuous-batching PR. Ugh. So tiny difference causing cross-region spill. Two fixes: revert comparator OR adjust scoring so local variants never lose to cross-region unless >1.05 penalty.

devex: UX note — console currently shows only final target. We should expose the fallback chain + scores in the per-request trace view so customers (and SRE) can see why cross-region happened.

ops-oncall: quick mitigation: disable cross-region fallback for region=EU for 30m and add a short circuit to prefer same-region variants for tier >= standard. I can flip the policy toggle.

alex: +1. Also adding a short-term circuit breaker for variant fallback when local utilization >0.9.

deploy-bot: config-change: apply toggle "disable_cross_region_fallback_eu" -> true by ops-oncall at 2026-03-17T10:18:12Z :hammer:

infra-bot: metric: cross_region_fallback_rate aux-us-west dropped from 4.3% -> 0.11% within 2m after toggle.

mira: OK mitigation looks good. Next: patch the comparator and add an integration test that simulates near-saturation so comparator logic won't regress. Also add an alert for >1% cross-region fallback for a region for >5m.

sam: I'll own the comparator revert + scoring change. Plan: revert to '>' then add a tunable penalty for cross-region in scoring. I will open a PR and put canary on staging first.

devex: I'll prototype the fallback-chain UI bits and add an entry in the rollout UX doc so product/console teams can review.

ops-oncall: creating incident ticket INF-2026-03-17-01. Will add impact notes: increased p95 latency for EU customers ~70ms, small percentage of requests routed cross-region.

alex: Can we also add a telemetry badge on the model catalog showing cross-region-fallback-rate per variant? Would make debugging easier.

mira: yes — add a tiny widget on model page + alert binding. I'll add to the observability roadmap.

sam: PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4721 comment: revert comparator + add cross-region penalty. Will attach perf bench.

deploy-bot: rollout: config 4721 staged -> canary (5% traffic) at 2026-03-17T10:45:00Z

infra-bot: canary metrics look good (no cross-region increase). Running the synthetic near-saturation test.

ops-oncall: leaving the emergency toggle in place for 1h post-rollout. If canary looks good, we'll remove toggle.

alex: thanks team. Postmortem notes: cause = comparator change in capacity check + scoring not penalizing cross-region enough; impact = minor latency increase for a subset of EU traffic and auxiliary region load spike; remediation = revert/patch + UI + alerts + test coverage.

devex: I'll add a console changelog bullet for customers affected and show how to opt into stricter per-tenant regional routing if they want maximum locality.

sam: postmortem draft incoming. Will include timeline, commits, and mitigations.

ops-oncall: closing the active incident when PR fully rolled out and toggle removed.

alex: closing thread here — thanks all. Follow-ups tracked in INF-2026-03-17-01 and PR 4721. :thumbsup:
